_comment: HAND-AUTHORED and NOT generated. Like Home, this is a virtual page: no clrType, no documents,
no collection. ForgeAccountsActions.OnLoadAsync scaffolds it per request.
This is D4 made navigable: ONE PAGE PER FORGE rather than one merged list. The forge arrives as
the program unit's objectId -- 'github', 'gitlab', 'bitbucket', the same canonical vocabulary
as document ids and routes -- and OnLoadAsync 404s on anything else rather than falling back to
a default, because a page that silently shows GitHub when asked for GitLab is worse than no
page. The accounts grid below is the SAME my-accounts query Home uses; MyAccountRowActions
narrows it from args.Parent, so there is one aggregation and one row shape, not two that drift.
Why a forge gets its own page at all rather than a column on a merged one: each forge's 'who
may manage this org' rule is genuinely different, so a merged table would put three different
meanings in one column with no way for the reader to tell which is which. See PRD 5.4.
Provider is isVisible:false -- the page is already about one forge and its breadcrumb says so,
so drawing the word again on the page body would be noise. It is present because the page
Read/ForgeAccounts is granted to the AUTHENTICATED role only, unlike Read/Home which anonymous
visitors also hold. There is nothing to show a signed-out visitor here: the whole page is the
caller's own accounts on one forge.

persistentObject.name: ForgeAccounts
persistentObject._aliasComment: Declared rather than derived. The client sends the alias as the objectTypeId on /spark/po/load, and the derived form would be 'forgeaccounts' -- the program unit says 'forge-accounts', and a mismatch 404s indistinguishably from a missing right.

attributes.name: Title
attributes._comment: Feeds the breadcrumb template only; never drawn as a row. The actions class sets Breadcrumb directly as well, so this is the fallback path rather than the primary one.

attributes.name: Provider
attributes._comment: The canonical lowercase spelling. This is what MyAccountRowActions reads off args.Parent to scope the grid, so it is the page's entire reason for existing -- not decoration.
